prechecks: Contain the identity before ordinary investigation: block or restrict sign-in and revoke active sessions/tokens through the approved identity-incident process.
Review Entra sign-in/risk evidence, recent MFA/security-info changes, registered authentication methods, privileged-role activity and suspicious OAuth/application consent.
Immediately after approved credential reset, inspect Exchange Inbox rules and mailbox forwarding using Get-InboxRule and Get-Mailbox ForwardingAddress/ForwardingSmtpAddress.
respond-to-a-suspected-compromised-accou.rollback: Re-enable the identity only after Security/IAM clearance, legitimate MFA methods are restored, malicious sessions/rules/forwarding are removed and the user validates normal access.

prechecks: Check the official cloud/provider health source before changing the gateway or internal network.
Check gateway connection/tunnel counts, platform health and recent configuration changes.
Confirm BGP peer state and IKE/IPsec tunnel phase/status from gateway logs.
troubleshoot-a-cloud-vpn-gateway.rollback: Export or capture the current gateway configuration before change; revert to the last known-good gateway configuration if connectivity worsens.

prechecks: Confirm gateway reachability and DNS resolution from the Linux endpoint.
Review journal/system/client VPN logs before changing the client.
Confirm system date/time and NTP synchronisation.
troubleshoot-linux-vpn.rollback: Record the current approved VPN client package/profile and restore the previous approved version/profile through package management or software distribution if the change causes regression.

prechecks: Check the managed VPN configuration and authentication settings before recreating the profile.
Check Keychain for the expected VPN certificate/credential objects without exporting secrets.
Test an approved alternate network to separate local-network failure from corporate VPN failure.
troubleshoot-macos-vpn.rollback: Preserve the approved VPN profile or MDM payload assignment and restore the original managed profile if the replacement causes regression.

prechecks: Check MDM compliance and whether the required VPN profile/app is assigned.
Confirm the installed VPN app version is organisation-approved.
Test cellular versus Wi-Fi where policy permits.
troubleshoot-mobile-vpn.rollback: Record the current managed VPN profile/app state and restore/redeploy the previous approved MDM profile if re-enrolment or app changes cause regression.

prechecks: Determine whether degradation is single-user or multi-user.
Check gateway utilisation, concurrent connections, packet loss and tunnel statistics.
Confirm whether split tunnelling, QoS or traffic-shaping changes are involved.
troubleshoot-slow-vpn-performance.rollback: Capture QoS, split-tunnel and traffic-shaping configuration before change and restore previous known-good values if performance worsens.

prechecks: Check VPN gateway/server authentication certificate expiry and chain before changing the client.
Confirm client and gateway system time are synchronised.
Check certificate revocation/trust state and required root/intermediate certificates.
troubleshoot-vpn-certificate-failure.rollback: Preserve the previous valid approved certificate/profile where supported; restore it if the replacement breaks authentication.

prechecks: Check gateway logs for IKE/IPsec rekey, Dead Peer Detection and session-timeout failures.
Check address-pool/session capacity.
Capture packet-loss/route behaviour during the disconnect window.
troubleshoot-vpn-disconnections.rollback: Record existing rekey/DPD/session values and restore previous stable values if disconnect frequency worsens; use the vendor-supported rollback mechanism for remote gateway changes.

prechecks: Verify the user's identity through the approved out-of-band verification process.
Check whether the lockout/failed-sign-in pattern indicates brute-force or suspicious activity.
Confirm required MFA/authentication methods remain available after reset.
password-reset.rollback: If access fails after the reset, use the organisation's approved temporary-access/recovery method rather than recycling or disclosing old credentials.

prechecks: Confirm corporate network/VPN connectivity.
Test the approved UNC path directly.
Check entitlement/group membership and capture current mappings with net use before deleting a mapping.
mapped-drive-missing.rollback: If remapping fails, remove only the mapping created during this procedure and restore the previously documented approved mapping.

prechecks: Check identity-provider/service health before changing MFA registration.
Review registered authentication methods and policy/Conditional Access requirements.
Confirm mobile device date/time and push-notification capability where relevant.
mfa-setup-fails.rollback: Before deleting an authentication method, record the approved recovery path; if re-registration fails, use the organisation's approved temporary-access method.

prechecks: Determine scope first: one endpoint, one platform, multiple users or gateway-wide.
Check provider/gateway service health before client remediation.
Check Conditional Access/NAC/identity blocks before deleting profiles or certificates.
vpn-not-connecting.rollback: This procedure is a triage parent; do not perform destructive profile/certificate changes here. Route to the child runbook that owns rollback.

prechecks: Verify approved requester/change authority.
Confirm group scope/type, nested membership and target entitlement.
Record existing membership state before the change.
add-or-remove-security-group-membership.rollback: If the change causes unintended access impact, restore the exact previous membership state and document the reversal.

prechecks: Check Microsoft 365/Teams service health.
Test Teams on the web to prove the issue is local to the desktop client.
Confirm which Teams client generation is installed before using a cache path.
clear-and-rebuild-the-teams-cache.rollback: Close Teams and preserve/rename relevant client cache/profile data before deletion where supported; restore preserved state or reinstall through the approved channel if rebuild fails.

prechecks: Make a byte-for-byte copy of the PST before any repair attempt.
Confirm Outlook is closed and the PST is on a supported local storage path.
Record file size and available free disk space.
recover-an-outlook-pst-file.rollback: Never repair the only copy. Restore the untouched backup PST if repair reduces recoverable data or Outlook can no longer open the file.

prechecks: Test Outlook on the web.
Check Microsoft 365 service health and mailbox quota.
Record the current Outlook profile/account configuration before removal.
repair-an-outlook-profile.rollback: Preserve the existing profile/configuration; restore the previous supported configuration if the new profile fails.

prechecks: Capture ARP/MAC evidence for the duplicate address before changing either device.
Check DHCP reservations/exclusions/leases.
Trace the conflicting MAC address to a switch port or managed endpoint where tooling permits.
resolve-a-duplicate-ip-address.rollback: Record both devices' original network settings and restore the previous known-good approved configuration if the corrective change causes loss of service.

prechecks: Review NAC/ISE/ClearPass or equivalent authentication/posture logs.
Check device compliance/MDM state before bypassing NAC.
Confirm VLAN/quarantine assignment and authentication result.
resolve-a-network-access-control-block.rollback: If a NAC policy change causes wider blocking, restore the prior approved policy; for a single device, re-evaluate posture and re-authenticate instead of bypassing controls.

prechecks: Confirm the endpoint has a 169.254.0.0/16 address and capture adapter/VLAN information.
Check DHCP scope availability and relay/helper reachability before assigning a static address.
Check switch-port/VLAN path if more than one device is affected.
resolve-an-apipa-address.rollback: Record existing adapter configuration and restore the approved DHCP/static configuration if remediation produces a worse network state.

prechecks: Step 0: isolate the affected endpoint through approved EDR/network controls when active compromise is credible.
Preserve EDR/AV, process, network and identity evidence before cleanup.
Check for suspicious outbound/C2 activity and wider scope from the security console.
respond-to-a-suspected-malware-infection.rollback: Release isolation only after Security Operations confirms containment/eradication criteria; destructive cleanup or restore requires an approved recovery point and incident-owner approval.

prechecks: Use domain-controller lockout evidence and approved lockout tooling/logs to identify the source system.
Check cached credentials on old endpoints/mobile clients and disconnected sessions.
Check services and scheduled tasks that may still use the old password.
trace-an-active-directory-account-lockou.rollback: Do not repeatedly unlock without fixing the source. If a service/task credential is changed, record the previous service configuration and restore only through the approved change path if the service fails.

prechecks: Test resolution against primary and secondary DNS servers from multiple network locations.
Check authoritative zone/forwarder/replication health before restarting DNS services.
Check server resource/query-rate anomalies and recent DNS changes.
triage-a-dns-service-issue.rollback: Export or record the affected zone/forwarder configuration and restore the previous known-good DNS configuration if resolution worsens.

prechecks: Check wireless controller/cloud registration state before rebooting the AP.
Check switch-port link/VLAN/trunk and PoE power budget before restart/replacement.
Check neighbouring APs to determine whether the outage is local or wider.
triage-a-wireless-access-point-outage.rollback: Capture AP/controller and switch-port configuration first. For remote Cisco IOS/IOS-XE switch changes, schedule reload in 10 and cancel only after verified recovery; use the vendor-equivalent rollback safety mechanism elsewhere.

prechecks: Check RADIUS/NPS/ISE authentication logs.
Check client certificate validity, chain and trust where certificate-based authentication is used.
Check switch/AP 802.1X configuration and RADIUS reachability.
troubleshoot-802-1x-authentication.rollback: Capture RADIUS policy and network-device configuration before change; revert the specific policy/configuration if authentication failures increase.

prechecks: Check captive-portal/NAC service health.
Check DNS/HTTP redirect path and portal certificate/URL reachability.
Check sponsor/guest approval workflow state where applicable.
troubleshoot-a-captive-portal.rollback: Capture portal/NAC configuration before change and restore the previous known-good portal policy/theme/redirect configuration if the change breaks authentication.

prechecks: Test the gateway from multiple endpoints on the subnet.
Check routed/SVI interface state and error counters.
Check first-hop redundancy state such as HSRP/VRRP/GLBP where implemented.
troubleshoot-a-default-gateway-failure.rollback: Before a remote Cisco IOS/IOS-XE routing/gateway configuration change, capture the current configuration and schedule reload in 10; cancel only after management and forwarding verification. Use the vendor-equivalent rollback mechanism elsewhere.

prechecks: Check firewall logs for the exact source, destination, protocol and port denial.
Verify the application's documented network requirements before adding a rule.
Check NAT/PAT and upstream security controls.
troubleshoot-a-firewall-blocked-applicat.rollback: Capture the current ACL/rule state; if the new rule causes unintended access, remove/revert only that change and restore the prior known-good policy.

prechecks: Use the canonical mapped-drive procedure instead of maintaining a second reconnect workflow.
troubleshoot-a-mapped-drive-reconnect-fa.rollback: Not applicable after deprecation; the canonical mapped-drive procedure owns rollback.

prechecks: Test reachability from a client and the print server where present.
Check printer panel/hardware state and switch-port/network link.
Confirm printer IP/hostname has not changed before reinstalling drivers.
troubleshoot-a-network-printer-that-is-u.rollback: Record current port/driver/queue configuration and restore the previous driver/port configuration if the change causes regression.

prechecks: Compare another authorised user/device to determine scope.
Check group membership plus share and NTFS permissions before modifying ACLs.
Confirm the file server/share is online and the exact UNC path is published.
troubleshoot-a-network-share-access-fail.rollback: Export or record the current ACL before change and restore the previous permission state if access or inheritance worsens.
